$1,000 into SanDisk a year ago is $31,000 today.
 
You missed that one. Jensen Huang says robots are the next AI trade, but the real money is not in the robots themselves. It is in actuators, the muscles and joints that make them move.
 
These are the kind of investing insights every trader and investor needs before trading the next supply chain bottleneck. Here is the full map.
 
Every joint in a humanoid needs an actuator, dozens per robot, together nearly half the cost. We mapped the entire supply chain looking for where the fewest companies control it. Bottleneck plus extreme demand is exactly how SanDisk went 31x.
 
The chain runs 5 layers deep.
 
It starts with rare earth magnets. No magnet, no motor, no movement. MP Materials ($MP) is backed by the Pentagon and runs America's only rare earth mine at scale.
 
Then magnets go into motors, which turn electricity into motion. Nidec is the world's largest motor maker, now building humanoid joint parts. AMETEK ($AME) is top 3 globally in the precision motors named in the Optimus chain.
 
A joint either rotates or pushes, like your shoulder and knee. Rotating joints need a reducer to turn fast, weak spin into slow, powerful force. Harmonic Drive Systems commercialized it, orders up 56% last quarter.
 
Pushing joints need a planetary roller screw, turning spin into a straight push like a piston. So precise each one costs up to $2,700. JP Morgan says screws and reducers alone make up a third of the robot. NSK is Japan's precision screw giant at just 17 times earnings. Schaeffler bought Swedish screw maker Ewellix and now sells directly into humanoids.
 
Finally it all gets assembled. Sanhua is Tesla's most-cited actuator partner, listed in Hong Kong last year.
 
Every layer has only a few suppliers, and demand is about to explode as humanoids mature. That is a textbook price explosion setup.
 
Comment ROBOTICS for the same AI agents we used to map this entire chain.

I did AI research at MIT and co-authored a technical paper on AI data-center sustainability & infrastructure. Iâm currently studying CS @ Cornell.

Research doesnât need a lab or a PhD. Every tool below is free and public, similar or exact to what is used in formal research.

Here are 10 projects that will stand out for research programs and technical roles on your resume -

interpretability:

1. Find induction heads in GPT-2. The classic first mech interp result. Thereâs a demo notebook that gets you there in an afternoon.
Tech: Python, TransformerLens.

2. Replicate the IOI circuit. Reverse-engineer how a model figures out who âhimâ refers to. Activation patching and logit attribution, the core toolkit.
Tech: TransformerLens, PyTorch.

3. Linear probe. Train a classifier on a modelâs hidden states to detect whether a fact is encoded before itâs spoken.
Tech: scikit-learn, TransformerLens.

4. Steering vector. Find the activation direction for a trait, inject it at inference, watch the output shift. Neuronpedia lets you try it in-browser first.
Tech: PyTorch, Neuronpedia, open-weight model.

training:

5. Train GPT-2 from scratch. Karpathyâs nanoGPT. One consumer GPU, a few hours.
Tech: PyTorch, nanoGPT, FineWeb.

6. Enter the NanoGPT speedrun. An open leaderboard for training GPT-2 to a fixed loss as fast as possible. Itâs gone from 45 minutes to under 90 seconds and every record is public.
Tech: PyTorch, modded-nanogpt.

7. Scaling law. Train the same tiny model at five sizes, plot loss vs parameters, get a straight line on a log plot.
Tech: PyTorch, matplotlib.

8. Ablation study. Delete one component at a time. Measure what breaks.
Tech: PyTorch, wandb.

evaluation:

9. Build an eval nobodyâs built. 100 test cases on a narrow skill plus the graders. Original benchmarks are genuinely scarce.
Tech: Python, pytest, model APIs.

10. Contamination check. Rewrite benchmark questions yourself and see if the score drops. If it does, the model memorized.
Tech: Python, any model API.

final: 

Write four pages on one of them. Abstract, method, results, limitations.
Tech: Overleaf, LaTeX, matplotlib.

Claude Fable 5 was asked a simple but unsettling question:

âYouâve studied every major psychology paper and the work of historyâs leading psychologists and philosophers. What are five truths people must understand about their own minds or risk failing in life?â

Its answers were brutally honest.

1. You are not a reliable narrator of your own mind. Research by Nisbett and Wilson showed that people often confidently explain decisions without recognizing what actually influenced them.

2. Environment is stronger than willpower. Highly disciplined people usually design their routines, surroundings, and defaults so the right choice becomes the easiest one.

3. You adapt to almost everything. Success stops feeling exciting faster than expected, while painful events often hurt for less time than feared. Meaning, connection, novelty, and progress tend to last longer.

4. Avoidance creates more suffering. Every difficult conversation or uncomfortable task you escape brings temporary relief, but often makes the fear stronger later.

5. You become shaped by your relationships. The Harvard Study of Adult Development found that close relationships are among the strongest predictors of long-term health and happiness.

The hardest part is not understanding these truths. It is knowing exactly which one you are ignoring and continuing to ignore it anyway.

Upside Down Sushi Cake. Recipe â

â  INGREDIENTS
For the sushi rice:
â¢ sushi rice - 1 1/2 cups (300 g)
â¢ rice vinegar - 3 tbsp
â¢ sugar - 1 tbsp
â¢ salt - 1 tsp

For the sushi bake:
â¢ sushi-grade salmon - 10-12 oz (300-350 g), diced
â¢ cream cheese - 8 oz (225 g), softened
â¢ avocado - 1, sliced (optional)
â¢ cucumber - 1 small, thinly sliced (optional)

For the pan:
â¢ avocado oil or neutral oil - 1-2 tsp

On top:
â¢ furikake or black & white sesame seeds
â¢ spicy mayo - for drizzling
â¢ green onion - finely sliced

To serve:
â¢ nori sheets

â  HOW TO COOK:
1. Rinse the sushi rice 3-4 times until the water runs mostly clear. Cook according to package instructions.

2. While still warm, mix the rice with rice vinegar, sugar, and salt (mix everything before adding it to the rice and stir the rice with a soft spatula to avoid turning it into mush). Let it cool slightly.

3. Lightly grease a bowl or deep dish with avocado oil (or another neutral oil).

4. Add an even layer of diced sushi-grade salmon.

5. Spread the cream cheese on top in an even layer.

6. Add sliced avocado and cucumber layers (optional).

7. Finish with the sushi rice and gently press everything down firmly with a spoon or damp hands.

8. Sprinkle a little more furikake or sesame seeds on top of the rice before flipping.

9. Let it sit for 2-3 min, then carefully flip it onto a plate. Lift the bowl slowly so the âsushi cakeâ drops out cleanly.

10. Drizzle generously with spicy mayo and top with green onion.
Scoop some onto a piece of nori and eat it like a hand roll.

Prep: 25 min  Cook: 20 min
Serves: 3-4

label_values.value:
A recent controvery has emerged on the internet regarding the fact that Witch Hat Atelier Mangaka copied it's many themes from Frieren & Dungeon Meshi.

But this claim falls apart when looking at the release dates of the mangas, which show Witch Hat Atelier predates Frieren by several years. Witch Hat Atelier was seriealized in July 2016,while Frieren was seriealized in April 2020. Witch Hat Atelier had been running for nearly four years before Frieren even released its first chapter.

The confusion likely comes from fans grouping these three titles together as the "Big Three" of Modern Fantasy. Unlike 90s Dark Fantasy mangas like Berserk & the recent ones like Demon Slayer/Made in Abyss, Fantasy mangas like Frieren/Witch Hat Atelier/Dungeon Meshi are wholesome, vibrant & often positively existentialist.

You may also see accusations that the character Qifrey (from Witch Hat Atelier) is a copy of Gojo Satoru (from Jujutsu Kaisen) due to their white hair and blindfold/glasses. This is also false; Qifrey's character design debuted in the manga in 2016, roughly 1-2 years before Gojo became a cultural icon with the JJK anime popularity, and the "blindfolded mentor" trope predates both.

When someone says âRAG over millions of PDFsâ
theyâre not asking about AIâ¦

theyâre asking about search + systems.

Hereâs what that actually looks like ð

Iâd break it into 5 parts: ingestion, embeddings, retrieval, generation, monitoring

1ï¸â£ Ingestion is offline, not request-time
At scale, this must be async

â¢ Stream documents from storage (S3/GCS)
â¢ OCR only when needed
â¢ Clean + normalize text
â¢ Chunk intelligently (not randomly)
â¢ Attach rich metadata (doc, page, section, etc.)

None of this should ever touch your user request path

2ï¸â£ Embeddings + indexing built for scale
You donât embed on demand

â¢ Batch embedding jobs (GPU or queued)
â¢ Distributed ANN indexes (Milvus, Qdrant, Vespa, Elastic)
â¢ Sharding + HNSW / IVF / PQ
â¢ Store metadata alongside vectors

Key insight:
metadata filtering is your first gate
vector search is the fallback

3ï¸â£ Retrieval + generation (tight path)
Your request path should stay minimal:

query â metadata filter â cache â ANN search â rerank â LLM

â¢ Most queries never even hit vector search
â¢ Many donât hit the DB at all (cache wins)
â¢ Rerank a small set only
â¢ Send 5â10 chunks max to the LLM

More context â  better results
More chunks usually hurt

4ï¸â£ Caching is everything
This is what controls cost + latency

â¢ Query â answer cache (FAQs, repeats)
â¢ Query â retrieval cache (top chunks)
â¢ Data/index cache (hot vectors, parsed docs)

Real path looks like:

query â cache â (miss) retrieve + LLM â write back

5ï¸â£ Monitoring closes the loop
Without this, your system silently degrades

â¢ Retrieval quality (recall@k)
â¢ Answer quality (feedback loops)
â¢ Latency + cache hit rates
â¢ Re-embed + re-shard as data evolves

BOTTOM LINE:

RAG at scale is NOT an LLM problem
Itâs a search + caching architecture problem

Most people are building demos
Real AI engineers are building systems

Youâre looking at a real neural network. Not the machine learning kind. The biological kind.
Everyoneâs building bigger models. Iâm building a brain.
I built a neuromorphic AI platform with 1 million spiking neurons, 11 brain regions, and 1.2 billion connections. It doesnât memorize training data. It learns continuously from real experience, the same way a biological brain does.

The reason I started building this is pretty simple. Every time an AI model gets smarter, it costs more energy, more hardware, more money. A single query to a large language model uses more power than running this entire brain for an hour. That math doesnât work long term, and I donât think brute force compute is how intelligence actually works in nature.

So I went the other direction. This system runs on a single CPU, uses less than 5 watts, and never stops learning. No retraining. No massive datasets. No data center. It forms its own concepts, builds associations between things it sees and hears, develops reflexes, and adapts to situations itâs never encountered before. All on its own.

The architecture is modeled after real neuroscience. Thereâs a sensory cortex for vision, audio, and touch. An association cortex that binds those signals together. A predictive layer that anticipates what comes next and pays more attention when itâs wrong. Motor cortex for movement and speech. A brainstem that manages energy and survival. Every connection strengthens or weakens based on experience. Nothing is hardcoded.

One thing I built in from the start is a safety kernel. Every motor command the brain generates passes through a safety supervisor before it can reach the real world. It checks joint limits, force thresholds, and collision boundaries. If something looks dangerous, the system triggers a reflex withdrawal before the action ever executes. The brain can learn freely, but it canât act without clearance. Thatâs not a feature I added later. Itâs part of the architecture.

Crispy chicken shawarma ð¯

Ingredients 

For the chicken:

2 lb boneless chicken thighs, cut into pieces 
Salt to taste 
1 tsp black pepper 
1/2 tsp red chili powder 
1 tbsp smoked paprika powder 
1 tbsp garlic powder 
1 tsp cumin powder 
1/2 tsp coriander powder 
1/2 tsp turmeric powder 
1 tsp onion powder 
1 tablespoon lemon juice 
2 tbsp whole milk greek yogurt 
1 tsp red pepper paste
1 tbsp tomato paste 
2 tbsp oil ( for marinating ) + more for cooking the chicken 

For the garlic sauce:

1/2 cup mayonnaise 
3 tbsp sour cream
1 tbsp lemon juice 
2 cloves fresh garlic, minced
Salt to taste
1 tbsp olive oil

For the shawarma glaze:

1/2 cup oil 
1 tbsp red pepper paste or tomato paste 
1 tbsp sumac 
Pinch of salt
2 tbsp pomegranate molasses 

For the sumac onion:

1 red onion, thinly sliced
Squeeze of lemon juice 
1 tsp sumac
1 tbsp parsley, freshly chopped 
Salt to taste 
1 tbsp oil

To assemble 

6 thin pita bread 
1 cup tomato, seeded and diced
French fries

Method:

Marinade the chicken: In a bowl, combine chicken with salt, black pepper, red chili powder, smoked, paprika, garlic powder, cumin, coriander, turmeric, onion powder. Add lemon juice, Greek yogurt, red pepper paste, tomato paste, oil.  Mix well until the chicken is fully coated. Cover and marinate for at least 2 hours, or overnight.

Make sauce: In a bowl, whisk together mayonnaise, sour cream, lemon juice, garlic, olive oil, and salt until smooth. Refrigerate until ready to use.

For the glaze : Mix oil, red pepper paste, sumac, salt, and pomegranate molasses in a small bowl. Set aside.

For Sumac Onions: Combine sliced onion, lemon juice, sumac, parsley, salt, and oil. Toss well and set aside.

Heat oil In skillet over medium high heat. Add the marinated chicken and cook in batches for about 8â10 minutes until fully cooked and slightly charred.

Assemble the Shawarma: Take the pita wrap. Spread garlic sauce, add chicken, fries, sumac onions, fries and diced tomatoes.ï¿½Roll the pita tightly into a wrap. Toast it in a skillet for 1â2 minutes on each side. Then, coat the wrap with shawarma glaze and cook until itâs golden and crispy, serve warm.

Build your tolerance â¤µï¸

Yes, your urge to breath isnât because your running out of oxygen. Itâs the levels CO2 in your blood telling your brain itâs time to breathe ð¨ 

And GUESS WHAT? As freedivers we train our CO2 tolerance so that our urge to breathe comes later. Save this for later ð¾

We can train this doing CO2 Tables: (always out of the water!)

Step 1: Find your baseline
- Lay down and relax.
- Take an inhale and hold your breathe
- Donât force it. Stop at the first strongest urge.
- Note down your time.

Step 2: Train at 50%
- Halve your initial time
- This is your CO2 training hold

Step 3: Simple CO2 table
- Lay down and relax for 2 minutes
- Relax doing normal breathing
- Take an inhale and hold your breathe
- Hold for 50% of your initial time
- Rest for 2 minutes
- Repeat 6-8 times
- Each round, shorten the rest by 15sec

Additional Tips ð¡
- Practice dry only in a comfortable space
- Inhale into both the belly and the chest
- Donât inhale 100%, maybe 90% full, you want to be comfortable during your hold
- Stop with major discomfort
- The goal is calm comfort, not pushing
- Only practice freediving with proper training 
- never hyperventilate, this can cause blackout and it's very unsafe

NEVER PRACTICE IN THE WATER ALONE ð¨
FREEDIVING TRAINING ESSENTIAL BEFORE TRYING ANY BREATH HOLD IN WATER 

By doing CO2 tables we are teaching our nervous system that the urge to breathe isnât an emergency, instead we are showing that we are in control, we are safe.

Ingredients:

Laziness hides behind fear of failure.

They move with what they have.

I havenât exercised in 6 years.
See how stupid that sounds?

You can be a sporty person, and do lots of sport. 
We all know that.

Many people arenât sporty people, and still exerciseâ¦. Because it is good for you. 

And yet!!

Â«Â I havenât read a book since schoolÂ Â» 

Is worn with such pride!

You do not have to be a reader or a book worm or a nerd or Â«Â into littÃ©ratureÂ Â» to read. 
I would argue reading is for the mind what exercise is for the body.

Your heart will keep beating for a while without both.
But without both, your life will be dull, un-stretched, unlived.

Â«Â But I donât know what to read.Â Â»

Read it all!! 

You werenât born listening to  your Spotify favourites on shuffle, you tailored your likes. 
Itâs the same.

And since Iâm here, Iâd like to make a case to bring back the classics. The classics should be a part of everyoneâs lives. 

Â«Â Oh but Iâm mostly interested in power dynamics, and business, and sales, and non-fiction.Â Â»

Christ.
Do you imagine The Count of Monte Cristo has nothing to teach you about money?

If you want to understand love: 
Well which one?! Because Love has many textures; but lucky for you, literature has mapped them all:

Read SÃ¼skind for the obsessive kind, 

Read Hanya Yanagihara for the unbearable kind,

Read Khalil Gibran for the spiritual, luminous kind,

Read Tolstoy for the ordinary-and-therefore-DEVASTATING kindâ¦

And Read Mary Oliverâs poems for the love that teaches you to pay attention, and to let small things change you.

And if youâre scrolling to counteract the doom acquired from scrolling, might I suggest reading
The Boy, the Mole, the Fox and the Horse.
Long live @charliemackesy. (Now some of you may not consider this a classic, but the classics werenât classics at the time of their writing.)

See where Iâm getting at?

Reading is exercise for the mind.
Reading is not a hobby. It is an necessity.
The classics are not homework. 
They are islands of knowledge you ought to take a dip in.

Brown Butter Apple Fritter Focaccia ð Iâve just posted the full how-to video which shows every step so go have a look!

To make it:

Prepare a batch of same-day focaccia dough (recipe/tutorial is page 22 in my cookbook or the first post on my page - pinned to the top left corner). Follow the recipe instructions up until itâs time to tip the dough into the tray. 

While the dough is proofing, make the cinnamon sugar butter filling. 

Filling:
1/2 cup (115g) salted butter, browned*
1/2 cup (100g) light brown sugar 
1.5 Tablespoons ground cinnamon 
1/4 teaspoon vanilla extract
2-3 apples, peeled and finely diced (youâll mix these in in two phases)

*You can use regular butter without browning it first but youâll get more complex caramel notes in the filling if you brown the butter first! Itâs worth the extra effort. See comments for how to! 

Mix the browned butter with the brown sugar, cinnamon and vanilla. Set aside. 

When the dough has finished proofing, line the parchment on the tray with 2 tbsp melted salted butter instead of olive oil. Transfer the dough to the tray (9x13 inch) and gently stretch the dough to edges. Mix 1/3 of the diced apples with half of the cinnamon filling, spread over the dough and fold up as seen in this video. Flip the dough over and cover to finish proofing at room temp for 1-1.5 hours.

Preheat oven to 215C/420F, place rack in lowest position.

Youâll need to warm up the cinnamon sugar butter to make it drizzling consistency again (it hardens as it cools). Mix with the remaining 2/3 diced apples, spread over the top of dough evenly and dimple in. 

Bake for 23-25 minutes.

While it bakes, whisk up the glaze:

125g (1 cup) powdered sugar 
2-3 Tbsp milk
Dash vanilla extract 
Sprinkle of cinnamon 

Drizzle over the focaccia once itâs out of oven, brush on top, sides and bottom (I do this by rubbing the bottom in tray thatâs been brushed with the glaze). 

Transfer to cooling rack for glaze to harden (about 15 mins!). #focaccia #applefritter #foodporn #breadmaking

The best cinematography trick for a beginner to master the cinematic look:

1. Camera Recording Settings: the first step of turning on your camera is going inside of the camera recording settings. Manually change the setting to 23.98 fps rather than 60 fps. This will help feel your footage to become an industry standard feeling and tone to your footage. 

2. Shutter Speed / Angle: the cinematic setting for your motion of still images to feel like a cinematic film is by changing it to 1/45 or 180Â°. This is a normal standard industry setting that will help your footage to have a cinematic tone of normal motion.

3. Aperture: the most cinematic look that Iâve been taught is having a T4 - T5.6 aperture to have the best combination of shallow, but slightly deep focus of your field of view that will enhance your contrast with your highlights and shadows. 

4. ND Filters: shooting 15 minutes before golden hour is enough preparation for the sunlight to have a soft tone, but also brings the highlights and the amount of luminance to be at its peak, but with an ND filter of 0.3-0.6, which is equivalent to 1 to 2 stops down can help your overexposures back down to your normal look of T4 - T5.6, therefore creating the consistent cinematic look to your footage.

5. Color Grade: the beginners guide to your cinematic look to your final look of your film or footage is by creating at least 4-5 different nodes to your Davinci Resolve. This is called a âtree branchâ method to allow each node to have its own category or layer: separate Primary, Log Primaries, Log wheel, High-Dynamic Range, and Curve wheel to have the best color palette results when exporting and posting your cinematic film.

The best cinematography trick for a beginner to master the cinematic look:

1. Camera Recording Settings: the first step of turning on your camera is going inside of the camera recording settings. Manually change the setting to 23.98 fps rather than 60 fps. This will help feel your footage to become an industry standard feeling and tone to your footage. 

2. Shutter Speed / Angle: the cinematic setting for your motion of still images to feel like a cinematic film is by changing it to 1/45 or 180Â°. This is a normal standard industry setting that will help your footage to have a cinematic tone of normal motion.

3. Aperture: the most cinematic look that Iâve been taught is having a T4 - T5.6 aperture to have the best combination of shallow, but slightly deep focus of your field of view that will enhance your contrast with your highlights and shadows. 

4. ND Filters: shooting 15 minutes before golden hour is enough preparation for the sunlight to have a soft tone, but also brings the highlights and the amount of luminance to be at its peak, but with an ND filter of 0.3-0.6, which is equivalent to 1 to 2 stops down can help your overexposures back down to your normal look of T4 - T5.6, therefore creating the consistent cinematic look to your footage.

5. Color Grade: the beginners guide to your cinematic look to your final look of your film or footage is by creating at least 4-5 different nodes to your Davinci Resolve. This is called a âtree branchâ method to allow each node to have its own category or layer: separate Primary, Log Primaries, Log wheel, High-Dynamic Range, and Curve wheel to have the best color palette results when exporting and posting your cinematic film.

What youâll wish you knew soonerâ¦ ð»

Itâs easy to say youâre not flexible. I said the same. Since then, I fractured my spine twice - and now Iâm more flexible than almost anyone around me.

Itâs not because I have good genetics. Itâs not because I know a stretch that you donât. Itâs simply because I know HOW to stretch, and itâs simpler than you thinkâ¦

1ï¸â£ FREQUENCY: Flexibility isnât just about how âstretchyâ your muscles are. Itâs your nervous system ALLOWING your muscles to relax.

To gain flexibility, you need to reach your nervous system you are safe and comfortable in these ranges of motion, and the best way you can do this is stretching OFTEN, and CONSISTENTLY.

The two day rule is the best method for progress. Itâs normal, and okay to miss a day. But never go two consecutive days without stretching - this is where youâll lose adaptations, especially at higher levels.

2ï¸â£ DURATION: I donât stretch for long. Stretching often is more important. But if you want to progress, you still need to be stretching for at least one minute per muscle group, ideally more.

This doesnât mean you should hold a stretch for one minute though - stretching for longer than 30s at a time brings about diminishing returns.

Instead, stretch for ~30s, rest, and stretch again. This prevents microtears forming and allows you to go deeper and gain flexibility each set.

3ï¸â£ SPECIFICITY: If you want flexibility for a specific skill, just stretching the muscle group isnât enough. Flexibility is specific, so your stretching needs to reflect this.

For backbends I donât just go into the bridge. I straighten my legs and lean massively into my shoulders, stretching them and simulating the angle my joints are at at the bottom of a hollowback.

You need to build STRENGTH in the antagonists (the muscles that shorten so the stretched muscle can lengthen) - these will help pull you deeper into the stretch if strengthen them enough.

What EVERYONE forgetsâ¦ ð»

Stop saying youâre not flexible. Anyone can instantly improve their flexibility. The only reason people think theyâre not flexible is because theyâre stretching wrong.

If youâre serious about recovering faster, staying injury free, mastering skills and gaining strength - you have to be doing these things right:

1ï¸â£ STRETCHING BEFORE TRAINING: If you want to increase soreness, injury risk and reduce force output - you should absolutely stretch before training.

You need to be warmed up to stretch safely and effectively - otherwise your muscles will be sensitive and less pliable (stretchy), making it much harder for them to lengthen and to improve your ROM.

Stretching after training will sustain a high blood flow to the muscles you trained, providing the nutrients necessary to repair and recover, whilst the heat produced from contractions will make it much easier and less painful to stretch your muscles.

The only stretches that donât negatively impact your workout are dynamic stretches, which will help prepare your muscles.

2ï¸â£ STRETCHING WITHOUT STRENGTHENING: Your muscles are like blue tack. Stretch a very thin piece, itâll quickly snap or get damaged. When it is thick and strong, it can stretch much further.

Weak muscles can be flexible - but accessing these ranges of motion is unsafe without the strength necessary to prevent them from overstretching.

This is the reason hypermobile athletes are much more likely to get injured. ALWAYS build strength alongside flexibility to stay safe and progress fast.

3ï¸â£ INCREASING FLEXIBILITY: If you stretch but donât gain flexibility, itâs not you - itâs how you stretch.

Make sure youâre always taking slow deep breaths during your stretch, that you avoid painful ranges of motion, and stretch for at least a total of one minute for each stretch (doesnât have to be in one set).

Do this consistently, and youâll GUARANTEE progress.

Funny Games (1997), directed by Michael Haneke, is a disturbing psychological thriller that confronts audiences with their own relationship to violence in cinema. The story follows a family held hostage by two polite yet sadistic young men, who torment them with a series of cruel âgames.â What makes the film truly unsettling is its refusal to provide comfort or escape, as it strips away the safety net viewers often expect in thrillers.

Haneke deliberately breaks the fourth wall, forcing the audience to question why they are watching and what it means to consume violence as entertainment. The performances are chilling in their calmness, making the cruelty even more unbearable. Funny Games is not an easy watch, but it is a bold and provocative film that lingers, leaving viewers disturbed, reflective, and deeply unsettled.

Garlic Chili Oil Spaghetti ð§ (aka Aglio e Olio)

Comment âRecipeâ and Iâll send you the full recipe card for free!!

Minimal effort, max flavor. Garlicky, lightly spicy, and impossibly comforting ð« 

Ingredients:
-8 oz (225 g) spaghetti
-1/3 cup extra virgin olive oil (plus 1 to 2 tbsp more if needed)
-8 garlic cloves, thinly sliced
-1 tsp red chili flakes (or 1 tsp finely chopped fresh chili without seeds)
-1 to 1 1/2 cups reserved pasta water
-1 whole parsley stem (for infusing)
-1/3 cup fresh parsley leaves, finely chopped
-Fresh lemon zest, for garnish (optional)
-Freshly grated Parmesan cheese, for serving (optional)

Instructions:
1. Bring a large pot of aggressively salted water to a boil. Cook spaghetti until al dente. Reserve 1 1/2 cups of the starchy pasta water, then drain.
2. While the pasta cooks, heat the olive oil gently in a large skillet over medium-low. Add the garlic slices and whole parsley stem, stir constantly until the garlic turns light goldenâ¦ not brown (about 3 minutes)
3. Stir in the chili flakes and a pinch of salt. Let them bloom for 30 seconds, then remove the parsley stem and take the pan off the heat.
4. Add about Â½ cup of the reserved pasta water to the skillet and stir/whisk vigorously to combine with the oil. Itâll start looking creamy and slightly thickâ¦ thatâs your emulsion forming.
5. Return the pan to medium-low heat and add the drained spaghetti along with another splash of pasta water. Hereâs the key: Toss everything aggressively with tongs for 1â2 minutes, drizzling in 1 to 2 more tablespoons of olive oil and a bit more pasta water as you go. Alternate between the two while tossing nonstop. The sauce should turn silky and glossy. If it looks dry or clumpy, add more water; if it looks thin, keep tossing.
6. Turn off the heat and stir in the chopped parsley. Taste and add a tiny pinch of salt if needed.
7. Plate immediately, spooning any extra sauce from the pan over the top. Garnish with lemon zest and a sprinkle of Parmesan if youâd like (add cheese after plating so it doesnât break the emulsionâ¦ not traditional, but worth it ð).

Hot Honey Garlic Salmon ð¯

Comment âRecipeâ and Iâll send you the full recipe card for free!!

Fast, flavorful, and addictively goodâ¦ sweet heat meets buttery salmon ð«¶

Ingredients
For the Salmon:
-0.8 lbs (400g) fresh salmon, cubed
-2 tbsp soy sauce (use low-sodium if preferred)
-1 tbsp rice vinegar
-2 tbsp olive oil
-5 garlic cloves, minced
-2 tbsp honey
-1 tsp garlic powder
-2 tsp onion powder
- 1 tsp black pepper
-1/2 tsp salt
-2 tsp paprika
-2 tbsp neutral oil (for searing)
-2 tbsp unsalted butter (for basting)
-1/3 cup green onions, thinly sliced (plus extra for garnish)
For the Sriracha Garlic Aioli:
-5 tbsp mayonnaise
-1 to 2 garlic cloves, minced
-1/2 lime, juiced
-1 to 2 tbsp Sriracha sauce

Instructions:
1. Remove the skin if needed, then cube the fillets into large bite-sized piecesâ¦ think forkable, not finger food. Pat them dry with paper towel.
2. In a bowl, combine the salmon with olive oil, rice vinegar, soy sauce, honey, minced garlic, and all the seasonings (paprika, garlic powder, salt, onion powder, black pepper). Marinate for as long as your patience lasts (even 1â2 minutes works), but the longerâ¦ the more flavor.
3. Heat neutral oil in a large skillet over medium to medium-low heat (err on the lower side as honey + soy = caramelization fast). Once hot, add the salmon and cook about 3 minutes per side until golden and sizzling. Save the marinade for later; itâs liquid gold.
4. Lower the heat to low, add butter, and pour in the reserved marinade. Simmer for 2â3 minutes to fully cook off any raw fish juices, basting the salmon with the buttery sauce. Top with 1/3 cup sliced green onions.
5. Stir together the mayonnaise, garlic, lime juice, and Sriracha. Taste and add more Sriracha if youâre feeling spicy.
6. Recommended plating: Build a cozy bed of fluffy jasmine rice, pile on the salmon, scatter more green onions on top like confetti, and drizzle generously with that dreamy aioli.

EP. 2 WHAT TO COOK FOR YOUR VEGAN GIRLFRIEND (or boyfriend or partner) - 
CREAMY MUSHROOM STROGANOFF

OKAY - ANOTHER BIG HITTER. MY ONLY NOTE - AS ALWAYS, BLEND THAT CASHEW CREAM TIL SMOOOOOOTH. Like as smooth as possible. Soak your cashews overnight if you have a weak blender. Also blend for long enough (COULD BE LIKE A MINUTE OR MORE OK). Seems obvious but the amount of people telling me itâs grainy and sucky is not ok. Follow the instructions or as nuocmama would say, it is now your recipe and not mine. LOVE YOU GOOD LUCK. QUESTIONS? DM ME.

CASHEW CREAM 
1 cup roasted cashews, soaked in hot water for at least 1hr then drained 
2 cups water
2.5 tbsp Massel beef-style stock powder (or any bouillon powder)
1 tbsp dijon mustard
2 tbsp apple cider vinegar

-
OTHER
3 tbsp vegan butter or olive oil
800g botton mushrooms
2 brown onions
5-6 cloves garlic, minced
1 tsp dried thyme
3 tbsp tomato paste + 1 tbsp for later 
1 tbsp apple cider vinegar, for later (but optional)
1 cup red wine 
1 tsp black pepper 
Up to 1 cup water, if needed

Serve with
Rice or pasta
Freshly chopped Parsley 

METHOD.
Blend all cream ingredients until incredibly smooth (read that again). Chop mushrooms (or donât! - I also like keeping small mushrooms whole for juicier mouthfuls), onion and garlic. Heat butter or oil in a large pot and cook onion and garlic til onions are soft. Add tomato paste, thyme and mushrooms and stir to coat all mushrooms until theyâre coated red - cook for 3 mins with lid on. Stir em. Another 3 minutes with lid on. Add wine and let mushrooms cook for a minute. Add cashew cream, pepper and cook down for 4-5 mins until stroganoff is a consistency you like (add the water if it gets too thick). Stir in the tomato pate and apple cider vinegar towards the end so you get a sharper sour-cream like zing! OR NOT. Taste before adding to see if itâs the vibes. (I find it always is). Stir in 1/2 cup chopped parsley. Serve with rice or pasta and garnish with more parsley to IMPRESS.

High Protein Frozen Burritos are the Ultimate Meal Prep

Meal prepping and freezing high protein burritos changed the game for me - and was actually the first âmeal prepâ content I ever made

I had honestly never meal prepped until I realized just how convenient having easy, high protein meals stocked in my freezer was. It made my life SO MUCH easier on days I didnât feel like cooking

Since I started posting frozen burrito recipes, Iâve received thousands of DMs showing your freezers stocked with 10, 20, 30 and even 100+ of my high protein burritos at a time

If youâre looking to enter the burrito meal prep game, here are my top tips (more in comments)ð

Freeze Your Burritos
- Storing frozen keeps burritos tasting their best, and allows them to last for months. It allows you to prep in huge bulk (think 20-30 burritos/meals at at time) without worrying about them going bad/going uneaten
- Wrap individually and freeze, or place burritos on a sheet pan and toss in the freezer uncovered (âflash freezeâ) and then add to a gallon sized bag. Flash freezing first keeps them from sticking together while freezing

Reheat Method
 - Remove your burrito straight from the freezer, wrap in a paper towel, microwave for 1.5-2 minutes to thaw (flip halfway) - the goal is to get the interior softened but not hot. Next, air fry (I usually do 375 degrees for 6-7 minutes), or pan fry until crispy. Your burritos will come out perfectly crisp (not soggy) and taste as good, if not better, than fresh

Slowly Stockpile
- You donât need to spend hours and hours prepping - start by making 1-2 of my recipes a week (which will usually yield 20-30 burritos/meals). Repeat weekly, rotating recipes based on preference, and youâll slowly build a huge stockpile of frozen meals. The concept is to be in a âmeal prep surplusâ - cooking more than you eat each week, until you eventually have enough meals to last for months

If youâre looking for recipe ideas - I have an entire chapter in my meal prep cookbook dedicated to high protein frozen burrito preps, and tons of recipes on my feed

We all struggle with feeling demotivated to study sometimes â yep, even medical students! ð

Hereâs what I learned over 4 years before med school that actually made me enjoy studyingâ¬ï¸:

1) Introduce âRandom Intermittent Rewardsâð
Science: Your brain reacts way more powerfully to unpredictable rewards than predictable ones.
Uncertainty triggers powerful dopamine spikes â the same effect that makes slot machines addictive.
Action: After each study session, flip a coin: heads = you get a snack, tails = you donât.
It keeps your brain guessing and craving the next session!

2) Use the 5-Minute Neuroplasticity Windowâ±ï¸
Science: The first 5 minutes of any task decide whether your brain âlocks in.â
Once you start doing, your brain flips from Default Mode Network (daydreaming) into Task Positive Network (focused work).
Action: Tell yourself that youâre just going to do it for 5 mins - read one line , write one sentence, etc.ð

3) Boost Adrenaline Before You Studyð
Science: Mild adrenaline (not panic) spikes norepinephrine, sharpening your focus and memory.
Action: Do 20 jumping jacks, a quick jog, or even splash cold water on your face before your study session. 

4) Friendly Competition with Friendsð©ð¼âð¤âð©ð»
Science: When youâre competing and emotionally engaged (e.g feeling pride, embarrassment, excitement), your brain treats the information as âimportant,â and locks it in stronger than if you were just reading alone
Action: Play kahoot, do blurting sessions, or quiz each other. Compete to see who can explain a concept accurately the fastest.

Studying shouldnât feel like a chore! Gamify your study session, build momentum and studying will feel like FUN in no time! :D

airfryer sticky soy pork belly bites +â¨garlicccâ¨fried rice (yes a garlic fried this rice) ð cus who doesnât love a bunch of garlic tossed into their rice (probs edward cullen)

Ingredients:

for pork:
400g pork belly, cut into 1-2 inch pieces
2 tbsp honey 
1 tbsp brown sugar 
2 tbsp oyster sauce
1 tbsp light soy sauce 
1/4 - 1/2 tsp chinese five spice
1 tsp dark soy sauce
Â¼ tsp black pepper
2 tsp garlic paste 
1/4 tsp salt
1 tsp shaoxing wine
1 tbsp honey (for basting)

For rice:
Enough garlic until your ancestors say stop (I used a whole head hehe), minced
2 tbsp neutral oil
2 spring onion, minced (whites and greens separate)
2 cups of cooked rice
1/2 tsp msg
Â½ tsp sugar
1 tsp light soy sauce

Toppins: greens of spring onion, minced chives, crispy garlic pieces, egg yolk

Method:
1. In a bowl, add all the marinade ingredients for the pork belly (excluding the 1tbsp of honey) mix and let it marinade for atleast 30 minutes
2. During this time you can cook your rice (but best to use day old rice for the fried rice)
3. In a pan, add oil and fry the garlic on medium-low heat to brown the garlic. When it starts to turn golden brown, strain the oil into a bowl, making sure to reserve the crispy garlic pieces. (the garlic will continue to cook once you strain so donât let it brown too much in the pan)
4. Once the pork has finished marinating, add into an airfryer basket (reserving the extra marinade in the bowl) and cook at 180ÂºC for 20 minutes or until cooked, making sure to take out and baste with extra marinade mixed with 1 tbsp of honey every 5 minutes until glossy, brown and crispy)
5. In the same pan the garlic was fried, over high heat, add the reserve garlic oil followed by the whites of the spring onion, stir fry for a few seconds until aromatic and begins to soften)
6. Add in the cooked rice and give it a mix. Then go in with the seasonings. Mix, taste and adjust to liking. 
7. Add back in little bit more than half of the crispy garlic into the rice and mix then plate up. Use remaining garlic as garnish and top with pork belly.

Joe McNallys book taught me this technique that allows you to get away with waaaay slower shutter speeds than thought before. 

It's all about how you hold the camera. Here are some other tips not mentioned in the video.

1. Keep everything tight. Keeping your elbows tucked in allows the camera to be closer to your center of mass, allowing a steadier shot. 

2. Take a breath and slowly press the shutter. breathing out as you take the photo will improve steadiness, as well as slowly pressing the trigger. Quick pressing will do you no good here.

Other things to mention: You need to use your left eye for this method to look through the viewfinder. some people prefer their right eye, so this might not be for you.  personally, I shoot with my tight eye, but I don't have any issues doing this, I find it quite comfortable, actually. 

The link sends you to an online version of this book, I've read it, and for photographers that are trying to get into flash setups, it's personally been a game changer. 

If you found this helpful drop a follow!

Ingredients:
1 packet of Chappagetti plus all the seasonings
1 packet of neoguri plus all the seasonings 
Ribeye steak, cut into chunks
1 tsp neutral oil
Â¼ tsp baking soda
1 tsp Oyster sauce
1 tsp light soy sauce
Pinch salt
Pinch Pepper
Â½ tsp sugar
Knob of butter
2 garlic cloves

Toppings: egg yolk, greens of spring onion, sesame oil, sesame seeds

Method:
- In a bowl, marinate the steak chunks for at least 15 minutes
- In a pan on high heat, add a little oil, add the steak chunks and sear each side for around 1-2 minutes, flip the pieces then add the butter and garlic cloves

- In a pot of boiling water, add both instant noodles and the vegetable packets, for accordingly to packet instructions (i cooked for just under 4 minutes)

- In the same pot or another bowl, add the cooked noodles, the chapagetti seasoning packet, Â½ or all of the neoguri seasoning packet and the oil packet from the Chapagetti, and pour in the noodle water while mixing until you get the consistency you like
- Add the beef pieces and juices in, give it a good mix before plating in a bowl topped with chopped spring onions, egg yolk, sesame seeds and a drizzle of seame oil. Enjoy!

One of the fastest ways to make your colors feel balanced, cinematic, and intentional
â is using a triadic color scheme.

Most beginners just bump vibrance or throw on a teal-and-orange look because theyâve seen it work for others.
But what actually makes an edit feel rightâ¦ is color harmony.
And the triadic method is one of the most powerful tools for that.

â¸»

Hereâs how it works:

A triadic color scheme uses three colors that are evenly spaced on the color wheel.
It creates a balanced, vibrant look â without feeling too saturated or chaotic.

Classic triads:
â Red + Yellow + Blue
â Orange + Green + Purple
â Teal + Coral + Mustard

What makes triadic grading so effective?
It gives you contrast and depth, without the visual tension of complementary schemes.

â¸»

How I use it in Lightroom:

â I use Calibration and HSL Hue sliders to shift the base colors toward the triad I want
â I adjust Saturation carefully â usually two strong colors and one more subtle
â I fine-tune Luminance to make sure one tone leads the eye (usually skin or subject)
â Then I use masking to separate the subject from the background and keep the scheme clean

Once I started grading this way, my colors stopped fighting each other â
and finally started feeling cohesive.

The ideal separation in range for the Pull Back phase.

Harder to see with the angles on the some of the videos, but itâs outlining about 90 degrees backward rotation. Not crossing this line means itâs less (with the hips more forward), hitting it or being close to it is a better backward rotation. 70-85/90 is good-excellent

This is just a guide and some can have a bit less and still be able to use the sequence well and hit hard. What this range allows is the stretch and usage of the forward torso rotators, and creates the space to come up and around on the ball (reverse s curve).

The problem is some athletes are told to rotate or open up but donât have the space or the ability to separate the rotation from the hips. So theyâll just turn the whole body as a unit instead of separating. The hips will have a natural tendency to straighten a bit in the air after toe off, and if the athlete doesnât have the separation ability (in range and movement) then they wonât be able to produce as much power. Theyâll still get momentum into the ball because they will be turning, but theyâll be turning the body more as a unit or just with less âtrueâ rotation, and not overlapping the actions in the Spiking Sequence.

The first drill is great to obtain some general separation from the hips and torso. Iâd recommend rotating back about 3 times (each breath youâll find new range) for a 2-3 sets and doing this daily or every other day to get the adaptation. It is also good to build strength in the backward and forward rotation (lots of exercises/drills in my feed). The second drill can help with the range and separating the movement, getting a feel for what it is like to only move the torso forward as well as keeping the arm patient and loaded. Youâre also engraining the Reverse s curve, having the arm come up and around.

A lot to it but hope this helps! Keep putting in the work ð

.
3 cups sushi rice, cooked
2 tbsp sushi vinegar
1/2 lb sashimi grade salmon, chopped
2 tbsp Japanese mayo
2 tbsp sriracha
2 tbsp of sliced chives
3 tbsp ponzu
1 Jalapeno, sliced

1. Season the sushi rice with sushi vinegar by mixing it through gently.
2. In a large bowl, mix together chopped salmon, Japanese mayo, sriracha, and chives. Chill the mixture.
3. Using an onigiri mold or clean wet hands, form the riceballs with salmon mixture in the center.
4. Preheat oil in a pan. Shallow fry each riceball on each side just until golden brown. Any longer and the filling will cook through.
5. Brush each side with ponzu, wrap with seaweed, garnish with more filling, and top with a slice of jalapeno. Enjoy!

Youâre wasting your time if you skip the basic drills and jump right into the more advanced stuff

Hereâs why:

The whole point of plyometric training is to train your stretch-shortening cycle

Which is your muscleâs ability to stretch and contract quickly immediately after to produce force. 

 Training this will help improve your:
- strength
- power
- speed
- agility
- muscle elasticity
- reduce injuries

However, a mistake most athletes make when they first started plyo training is skipping the basic drills and jumping right into the more advanced drill

Which seems more challenging, fun or âsport specificâ

But the best way to start training your stretch-shortening cycle more effectively is simply mastering the pogo hops

as it teaches you foundational mechanics 

that help improve ankle stiffness, proper landing technique, and strengthen tendons.

Skipping this step and jumping right into more advanced drills will only lead to ineffective training 

as your muscles are not stretching and contracting rapidly enough to yield the adaptation. 

So start with pogo hops and build up from there.

Key tips when doing the pogo hops:

â Ankles stiff: Focus on quick rebounds using your ankles, not your knees.

â Minimal ground contact: Bounce lightly and quickly off the ground.

Comment "HACK" to get 7 MORE practical life hacks that will save you money! ð°

College is expensiveâ¦ BUT only if you donât try this! â¤µï¸

There are a couple main expenses you have to worry about during college.

Housing, Tuition, Food, Supplies.

Letâs tackle them one by one.

1. Housing

Thereâs not too much we can do about this other than commuting or becoming an RA (residential assistant). Most 1st and 2nd year are required to dorm so these expenses are likely fixed until you are able to move in with roomates. If you can/want to, consider commuting from home, becoming an RA (you get meals and housing compensated) or going to community for 2 years then transferring.

If youâre not dorming, spend alot of time looking into housing, as early as possible. the best deals always go away the quickest. also make sure to take a pic of the house before you move in, and live with as many roomates as possible

2. Tuition

Depends on what school youre going to but this is the worst expense by far. but you can do a couple things. Apply for scholarships, there are thousands of dollars that are allocated to scholarships that are never even applied for. take the time and apply to as many as possible. 

In HS, take as many AP classes or dual enrollment classes at your local community class. 

You can also take college courses during college over the summer/winter in community college. these classes will be alot cheaper and easier too. Only available mostly for GEâs.

3. Food

Unless you have a meal plan, learn to cook. If you eat out everyday, which it is extremely easy to do in college, you will burn through cash. make your own coffee, cook your own food. try not to snack a ton and donât waste money on expensive shots.

4. Supplies

This video is mainly about the supplies. abuse student discounts, never pay full price for textbooks, and always look for used supplies on FB marketplace. 

LMK if im missing anything!

Hi, missed you ð hereâs some chocolate cherry pancakes !!! Recipe below! 

Ingredients: 
-2 cups flour 
-2.5tbsp sugar 
-1.5tsp baking powder 
-1.5tsp baking soda 
-1tsp salt 
-dash of cinnamon 
-2 cups buttermilk 
-2 eggs 
-3tbsp melted unsalted butter (plus more for cooking) 
-1 cup quartered and pitted cherries 
-1/3c ish chopped dark chocolate 
-whipped cream: heavy whipping cream, powdered sugar, vanilla bean or vanilla extract, salt 
-cherry sauce: 2 cups halved and pitted cherries, 1/3cup water, 1/2tbsp cornstarch, 1tbsp lemon, 1/2tbsp sugar (or more if you want it sweeter) 

Recipe: 
-in a large bowl whisk together flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda, cinnamon, and salt. To the middle add melted butter, buttermilk and eggs. Whisk to combine (dont over mix). Fold in cherries and chocolate. Set aside for 30 min 
-heat a pot on med heat. add 1cup cherries, corn starch, water, lemon, and sugar. Slowly add cherries and stir until it thickens. Cook until cherries are softened and thereâs a syrup consistency (about 10min). Add water as needed 
-heat a pan on med-low. Add butter and 1/3c of pancake batter. Once bubbles form on the top, flip. Cook each side until golden brown 
-whisk together 1-2cups heavy whipping cream, vanilla bean (or 1-2tsp vanilla extract), pinch of salt and 1-2tbsp powdered sugar. Whisk until firm peaks form. Taste and adjust to your liking! Tip: make sure heavy whipping cream is COLD (you can also add to the freezer) 
-top pancakes with cherries and whipped cream!! Enjoy! 

*pancake batter adapted from The NY Times recipe :)

Hereâs a full body mobility routine - make sure to save this ð

1. Hip CARs: 4-5 reps
2. Shoulder Swimmers: 5-8 reps 
3. Neck Extension/flexion 5-8 reps
4. Thoracic Rotations: 5-8 reps
5. Scapula Controlled Articular Rotations: 5-8 reps
6. Spinal Segmentation: 3-5 reps
7. Knee Rotations: 5-8 reps
8. Ankle/Toe Kinetic Stretch: 5-8 reps
9. Elbow Controlled Articular Rotations: 4-6 reps
10. Wrist Extension/Flexion: 5-8 reps

To try a follow along hip and shoulder class, comment: CLASS

When doing these movements- the goal isnât to copy my range of motion, but instead, work within your own available ranges. Itâs okay if your range looks smaller or different. Also, only work in pain-free ranges of motion. Discomfort is completely normal, but avoid ranges where you feel a pinch, twinge, or sharp pain.

Make sure to do these slow and controlled with good focus. I also utilize internal tension throughout the movements. 

You can do this routine every single day if desired. The amount of sets is dependent on the individual, but you can start off with 1 set of everything. You can build up to multiple sets, or do 1 set of everything and a few sets on specific areas of need.

Uncomfortable Questionsð

6+ Million of you watched part 1, and I received so many messages for a part 2, so here we go:

1. If money was not a limit and failure was not a concern, what would you pursue passionately in your life? Is this different from what you are currently pursuing?

2. Be honest: Are there any toxic relationships or friendships in your life that you need to let go of for your own well-being? If so, when & how will you do it?

3. Are you living authentically, or are you trying to conform to other peopleâs expectations & opinions? What is the last time you put something off that you really would like to do yourself?

4. If people speak at your funeral, what values of you do you want them to highlight? Are you currently behaving in a way that will make this happen?

5. If you could rewrite your life story, what plot twist would you introduce, and how would it change the narrative? In what way can you work towards that narrative, starting today?

6. Who, what & when was the last person, experience or event that truly hurt you? Why did it hurt so much? What lessons can you learn from them? How can you implement them today?

7. If the 3 people closest to you, would die tomorrow, what would you regret not saying to them? Will you say it soon? 

Make sure to save this post, so that you can revisit them at a later moment.

Knowing yourself is the beginning of all wisdom. Self-reflection can be a very useful tool for this. It can be painful or confronting at times, but it can also be an anchor in the chaos we call: life.

Spending time in the air is something I always longed for. I considered it some sort of hidden superpower. Maybe because our human forms did not allow it if not for brief moments, maybe because in it are hiding the symbols of liberation and transcendence from the physical form. 

Either way, improving air sense always gave me an expansive sensation of control over my whole body, with readiness and quickness, and a grasp of situational awareness. That sensation that regardless of what would happen, my body would now have the wisdom to deal with it, and not get injured â growing rich with lightness and elasticity.

As in most fields that I explored I didnât want to pursue this direction through intensity alone (as in getting more powerful), as I know how boring it can get, how grey, how far from the complex human dimension. So, I continued this aerial pursuit through acrobatic maneuvers of all kinds, diverse jumping challenges, dives into water and so forthâ¦

Here in video you can see some riddles that support that difficult dimension that are yet available to everyone. Enjoy the process of building them up. Start with 4 singles each and over time build up to 3 series of 6 consecutive repetitions for each. Rest a lot in between each exercise, definitely no less than 2 mins.

Enjoy rooting in the skies everyone!

1. Feynman Techniqueð§âð«
Feynman Technique is a learning strategy that was developed by physicist Richard Feynman. The technique involves four steps: (1) Choose a concept you want to understand, (2) Teach it to someone else, (3 Identify gaps in your understanding, and (4) Review and simplify. By explaining the concept in simple terms, you can identify any areas where you donât fully understand the topic. 

2. Spaced Repetition and Active Recallâð¼ 
These are two techniques to improve memory retention. Spaced repetition involves repeating information at increasing intervals of time. The idea is that by spacing out the review of information, you can more effectively retain it in long-term memory. Active recall involves recalling information from memory without looking at notes. 

3. Accountability Partnerð¬
An accountability partner is someone who shares goals with you and helps you stay on track by checking in regularly. I prefer having a classmate as my partner. The idea is that by having someone to hold you accountable, you are more likely to follow through on your plans and make progress towards your goals. This can help you overcome procrastination and increase motivation. 

4. Power Napð
A power nap is a short nap, usually lasting 20-30 minutes, that can help you recharge your batteries and increase productivity. Itâs important to make sure that the nap doesnât disrupt your sleep cycle.

5. Deep Workð§âð»
Deep work is a term coined by author Cal Newport to describe focused, distraction-free work that requires intense concentration. The idea is that by eliminating distractions and working on tasks that require deep thinking and focus, you can produce higher quality work and accomplish more in less time.

Just when I was walking around the mall thinking what should I make, I walked pass a bakery and saw a mango cheesecake and I was like, âthatâs it!â Bought the ingredients, went home and got to workð¥­â¨

Maybe because itâs mango season right now, the mangoes are really really sweet. I bought more mangoes cuz thereâs another mango recipe imma be posting soon ~ ð if sheâs a big fan of mangoes, definitely give this one a try! 
.
Hereâs the super simple recipe for the mango cheesecake

Ingredients 
.
Cream Cheese - 250g
Whipping Cream (35%) - 200g
Icing Sugar - 50g
Mango Puree - 40g
Biscoff / Speculoos Biscuits - 80g
Melted Butter (Unsalted) - 25g
Mango - adjustable to your liking 

1. Blend or punch the biscuits to small pieces and combined with the melted butter. 
2. Flatten the biscuits in the bottom of the container and place in fridge for 1 hr 
3. Whip up the cream until stiff peaks form. 
4. Whip together cream cheese and icing sugar as well as the mango puree and combined with the whipped cream. 
5. Layer the mixture in the container with mango pieces inside and top off with more mangoes.
6. Place in the fridge overnight for it to set and enjoy ~ ð¥­â¨

label_values.value:
âQuestion of the day: Where are the support playersâ

Todays Build is Slowing Tahmkench Support. With his rework, Tahm moved a bit out of the support role into a solid toplaner. This Build puts him back in his supportive role by unleashing way too much cc on the enemy ADC/Support. For runes go glacial to get a huge slow to either easily hit your W easier or get a better engage/escape. For mythic item you wanna go Frostfire for some more slowing. The nex three items you wanna get to slow even more are rylais, randuins and deadmans. all items allow you to slow the enemy so no one has a chance of escaping. For the last item you can build waht works best for you (probably some MR). Since you stack HP and resistances, you deal good damage and are almost unkillable. If youneed some more damage, titanic hydra is the go to.

Give it a try and as always: these builds are for fun, to play in low Elo on a smurf or so. Some of them will work in high Elo too but some are just a bit troll.
If you play this build send me a pic of the results or post them in your story and link me and I'll post it backð.

âQuestion of the day: Nerv healing or buff antiheal?â

Todays Build is Max Healing Yone Midlane. And yea this build is a bit over the top with all the healing since yone already heals like crazy with his normal build. The intention of this build is to build as much healing stuff on him as possible. Thats why we chose conqueror as keystone rune (i know that lethal tempo probably is stronger on him, but conqueror gives you some more healing). For mythic item you go shieldbow and as second item BT for more damage and the crit. For the real  Max healing yone you go as last 3 items Spirit, Ravenous and bork in the order you want. If you want some more damage you can go IE or you go death dance for some more survivability.

Give it a try and as always: these builds are for fun, to play in low Elo on a smurf or so. Some of them will work in high Elo too but some are just a bit troll.
